title: Heterogeneous biased flip probability
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. For a coordinate $i$, the heterogeneous biased flip probability of $f$ at $i$ is the probability, under the product distribution on sign vectors whose coordinate signs have biases specified by $p$, that flipping coordinate $i$ changes the value of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: Each coordinate bias $p_i$ lies strictly between $0$ and $1$
$f$ maps sign vectors of length $n$ to signs
caveat: The snippet does not define the heterogeneous biased sign distribution or its convention for the bias parameters, so the probability measure cannot be specified more precisely from the given payload.
